beats.speaker: tilly-space
beats.voiceover: Ice everywhere. I'm standing on Enceladus, one of Saturn's moons.

shots.place: standing on the bright white-and-blue ice plain of Enceladus, soft rounded craters around her, black starry sky above, Saturn with its rings huge in the sky behind her
shots.action: standing steadily on the ice, turning calmly to the camera
shots.line: Ice everywhere. I'm standing on Enceladus, one of Saturn's moons.

beats.speaker: tilly-space
beats.voiceover: This whole moon is only about five hundred kilometres wide. And it's so bright, it reflects almost all the sunlight that hits it.

shots.sound: near silence, the soft crunch of ice and her steady breathing in the helmet

shots.place: standing on the bright white-and-blue ice plain of Enceladus, soft rounded craters around her, black starry sky above, the ice glittering brilliantly white in the sunlight
shots.action: standing still, shielding her visor with one hand for a moment
shots.line: And it's so bright, it reflects almost all the sunlight that hits it.
shots.sound: near silence, the soft crunch of ice and her steady breathing in the helmet

beats.speaker: tilly-space
beats.voiceover: Saturn hangs right there in the sky. It never moves. Down south, there are long cracks in the ice called tiger stripes. And they spray giant jets of ice into space.

shots.place: the icy horizon of Enceladus with the enormous ringed planet Saturn hanging low in the starry sky, filling a large part of it
shots.action: a slow, gentle pan across the horizon up to Saturn
shots.line: Saturn hangs right there in the sky. It never moves.
shots.sound: near silence, the soft crunch of ice and her steady breathing in the helmet

shots.place: a long, deep blue crack in the white ice running away toward the horizon, frost crystals sparkling along its edges

shots.line: Down south, there are long cracks in the ice called tiger stripes.
shots.sound: near silence, the soft crunch of ice and her steady breathing in the helmet

shots.place: tall white jets of ice spray shooting high up from long blue cracks in the ice into the black starry sky, glittering in the sunlight, Saturn in the background

shots.sound: near silence, the soft crunch of ice and her steady breathing in the helmet

beats.speaker: tilly-space
beats.voiceover: The catch? Under all this ice, there's a whole ocean of liquid water. Some of the spray even ends up feeding one of Saturn's rings.

shots.line: The catch? Under all this ice, there's a whole ocean of liquid water.

beats.speaker: tilly-space

claims.claim: Enceladus is about 500 km (about 313 miles) across.
claims.source: NASA Science, Enceladus, https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/moons/enceladus/ (about 313 miles / 504 km in diameter)

claims.claim: Enceladus's fresh, clean ice reflects almost all the sunlight that hits it; it is one of the most reflective bodies in the solar system.
claims.note: Bond albedo about 0.8, geometric albedo above 1; said as 'almost all'.

claims.claim: Enceladus is tidally locked to Saturn, so from its Saturn-facing side Saturn stays in the same place in the sky.
claims.source: NASA Science, Enceladus, https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/moons/enceladus/ (synchronous rotation) ; Online Astronomy eText, https://cseligman.com/text/moons/enceladus.htm
claims.note: True for the Saturn-facing hemisphere; the shots show that side.

claims.claim: Near Enceladus's south pole are long parallel fractures nicknamed 'tiger stripes', found by Cassini in 2005.
Jets (plumes) of water vapour and ice grains spray from the tiger stripes into space.
claims.source: NASA Science, Enceladus, https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/moons/enceladus/ ; AAS Nova, 'Geysers from the Tiger Stripes of Enceladus', https://aasnova.org/?p=336

claims.claim: Enceladus has a global ocean of liquid salty water beneath its icy shell.
claims.source: NASA Science, Enceladus, https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/moons/enceladus/ (Cassini gravity and libration data, 2015)

claims.claim: Material from Enceladus's plumes supplies Saturn's E ring.
Enceladus's surface is about minus 200 °C (around -198 to -201 °C).
claims.source: NASA Science, Enceladus, https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/moons/enceladus/ (about -330 °F / -201 °C) ; HyperPhysics (-198 °C at noon)

publish.title: I stood on Saturn's icy moon
publish.description: A moon 500 km wide that shoots giant jets of ice into space and hides a whole ocean under its ice. Tilly reviews Enceladus.
